sections.title: Reading the console
sections.description: Coverage, confidence, and track state answer different questions.

items.title: Coverage comes first
items.body: Healthy sensors with no detections mean quiet sky. Unhealthy or missing sensors mean the sky is not being observed reliably.

items.title: Confidence is explainable
items.body: Evidence combines with noisy-OR. Track detail shows each contributing class, count, weight, and last observation; confidence is never a threat score.

documents.title: Wi-Fi sensor
documents.summary: Passive monitor-mode capture and parsing for Wi-Fi Remote ID, DJI DroneID, and fingerprints.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.description: This is the current hardware path that can observe the DJI aircraft.

items.title: Capture
items.body: Listens to management beacons through a monitor-mode interface and never associates with, transmits to, or disrupts nearby networks.

items.title: Decode
items.body: Parses ASTM F3411 OpenDroneID messages and DJI vendor information elements into normalized Detection records.

items.title: Publish
items.body: Emits detections and regular health heartbeats over ZeroMQ so quiet sky remains distinguishable from sensor failure.

items.title: Channel occupancy
items.body: Reads the driver's own per-channel busy time and noise floor between dwells and publishes them on the heartbeat, for the 2.4 and 5 GHz bands the SDR cannot tune. Measured on this unit's mt7921u the driver reports nothing usable in monitor mode, so the panel says so rather than drawing an empty band; the path remains for adapters whose drivers do maintain these counters.

documents.title: Fusion service
documents.summary: Correlates immutable detections into stateful tracks with identity precedence and explainable confidence.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.description: Fusion is the only service that decides which observations belong to the same aircraft.

items.title: Identity precedence
items.body: Serial number wins, MAC address is the fallback, and a MAC-keyed track is promoted without losing history when a serial arrives.

items.title: Lifecycle
items.body: Tracks move through TENTATIVE, CONFIRMED, COASTING, and CLOSED. Reacquisition keeps the same track identifier.

items.title: Confidence
items.body: Distinct evidence classes combine using noisy-OR. Repeated observations within one class increase count, not weight.

items.title: Track lifecycle
items.body: CLASSG_FUSION_SENSOR_STALE_AFTER, CLASSG_FUSION_TRACK_TTL, and CLASSG_FUSION_REAP_INTERVAL control coasting, closure, and cleanup cadence.

documents.title: Go API
documents.summary: REST, GraphQL, WebSocket, persistence, capture and sweep control, health aggregation, and static UI delivery.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.description: The API remains available when radios or fusion are down so it can report degraded coverage.

items.title: REST and stream
items.body: Versioned endpoints expose tracks, detections, sensors, health, telemetry, captures, spectrum sweeps, configuration, and a live WebSocket stream. The stream sends only the topics a client subscribes to.

items.title: GraphQL
items.body: One read-only viewer-level endpoint at /api/v1/graphql answers nested questions such as tracks with their detections in a single round trip. Writes and the whole administration surface stay on REST.

items.title: Sessions and roles
items.body: Opaque session cookies over three ordered roles: viewer reads, operator acts on captures and sweeps, admin configures the machine. Optional OIDC single sign-on sits alongside local accounts.

items.title: Storage
items.body: Embedded libSQL is the local default with optional Turso synchronization; an in-memory backend supports development and tests.

items.title: Static application
items.body: The built Vite bundle is served with SPA fallback, while missing assets retain real 404 responses.

items.title: Health is public
items.body: GET /health and /metrics answer without a session, because a unit that reports its health only to authenticated callers cannot be watched by the thing that notices it died. Neither carries positions or identities.

sections.title: Environment variables
sections.description: API configuration is grouped by server, storage, streams, operations, retention, sign-in, and host agents.

items.title: Server and storage
items.body: CLASSG_LISTEN, CLASSG_VERSION, CLASSG_STORE, CLASSG_DB, CLASSG_TURSO_URL, CLASSG_TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN, and CLASSG_TURSO_SYNC_INTERVAL configure the process and database.

items.title: Streams and health
items.body: CLASSG_TRACK_ENDPOINT, CLASSG_DETECTION_ENDPOINT, topic variables, CLASSG_EXPECTED_SENSORS, and CLASSG_SENSOR_STALE_AFTER define live inputs and coverage health.

items.title: UI and capture control
items.body: CLASSG_UI_DIR, CLASSG_CAPTURE_DIR, CLASSG_SENSOR_WIFI_DIR, CLASSG_PYTHON, CLASSG_CAPTURE_ALLOW_UNPRIVILEGED, and CLASSG_SENSOR_RESTART_COMMAND configure operator actions.

items.title: Privacy and retention
items.body: CLASSG_EXPOSE_OPERATOR_LOCATION, CLASSG_RETENTION_DETECTIONS, CLASSG_RETENTION_TRACKS, CLASSG_RETENTION_TELEMETRY, CLASSG_RETENTION_SWEEPS, CLASSG_RETENTION_INTERVAL, CLASSG_MAX_HISTORY, and CLASSG_LOG_LEVEL govern exposure and storage bounds.

items.title: Sign-in and mail
items.body: CLASSG_AUTH_MODE, CLASSG_SESSION_TTL, the CLASSG_OIDC_ variables, and the CLASSG_SMTP_ variables are bootstrap rather than database settings, so a unit cannot have its own authentication switched off through its own web interface.

items.title: Host agents
items.body: CLASSG_SDR_BIN names a sweep binary the API may execute directly; CLASSG_DEPLOY_STATE_DIR is the directory shared with the host deploy and sweep agents. Each is empty by default and the affected feature reports itself unavailable rather than failing.

documents.title: Operator UI
documents.summary: A static React and MapLibre console for live airspace, evidence, history, spectrum, health, captures, and administration.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.description: Every view is designed around evidence and coverage rather than invented threat labels.

items.title: Live map
items.body: Plots aircraft, operators when supplied by policy, trails, range rings, and visually distinct ADS-B traffic, beside a resizable detail pane.

items.title: Tracks and evidence
items.body: Shows identity, lifecycle, position history, RSSI, and the exact evidence behind confidence.

items.title: Timeline
items.body: Reads recorded history back: what was seen, when, and which sensor saw it, over a window rather than the live moment.

items.title: Spectrum
items.body: Two sources, because no one radio covers the band. The SDR sweeps sub-2 GHz and returns power per frequency bin; the Wi-Fi adapter reports per-channel busy time across 2.4 and 5 GHz, which the SDR cannot tune. Both measure, neither identifies.

items.title: Operations
items.body: Sensor health, capture workflow, configuration editors, and this documentation are available without a Node runtime in deployment.

items.title: Administration
items.body: Accounts and sessions, outbound hooks and their delivery history, deployment status and control, and the host watchdog, all gated on the admin role.

items.title: Live by default
items.body: Views follow the WebSocket rather than waiting to be reloaded, banners about finished work close themselves, and a newly deployed build applies itself once nothing is mid-sweep or mid-capture.

documents.title: SDR sensor
documents.summary: Rust scaffolding for ADS-B context and sub-2 GHz energy and cadence detection.

sections.title: Architecture and hardware
sections.description: The RTL-SDR V4 tunes only to about 1.766 GHz.

items.title: What it can see
items.body: ADS-B, 433/868/915 MHz control links, 1.2/1.3 GHz analog FPV, and GNSS L1 interference indicators.

items.title: What it cannot see
items.body: DJI OcuSync at 2.4 and 5.8 GHz is physically outside tuner range. Gain or antennas cannot change that.

items.title: Privacy boundary
items.body: Future sweep logic characterizes envelopes and cadence only; it must never demodulate payload or video content.
